articles.title: Gems: a spending plan that protects your next upgrade
articles.summary: Target one progression milestone, use the right shop currency and stop buying when the reward is secured. A practical budget for gear, heroes and events.
articles.body:
## Choose what your next gems must achieve
Write down one reachable target: a hero star breakpoint, another etched slot, a missing gear piece or a specific event reward. Compare purchases against that target before buying. A discounted item that does not advance it can still delay your upgrade.

## Use the appropriate resource first
1. Gear direction: use Mythstone keys for your chosen starter set. The November 2026 beginner guidance explicitly preserves gems for other progression opportunities.
2. Hero progression: compare the guild-shop route toward your chosen rare hero's six-star milestone before spreading resources across several heroes.
3. Etched slots: compare blessing-rune purchases in the relevant shops. After the third slot, reassess instead of buying runes automatically.
4. Event reward: count earned resources and remaining free tasks before buying extra dice, lures or other event items.

## Decide: buy, wait or skip
- Buy: the exact item completes a useful milestone, the full cost is known and it fits your limit.
- Wait: free tasks can still reduce the shortfall, guild bargaining is unfinished, or overlapping event tasks have not been announced.
- Skip: the purchase only raises displayed power, belongs to a build you cannot yet assemble, or requires chasing an unknown random outcome beyond your limit.

## Set a stopping rule before an event
Choose a gem ceiling you can afford without delaying your priority upgrade. Subtract resources already held and expected free resources from the event target; do not copy someone else's total gem bill. Buy in small batches, update your actual reward balance and stop as soon as the target is reached. Fishing tasks changed in the historical discussion, so old budgets are not current prices.

## Compare offers correctly
Divide price by bundle size only for equivalent items paid in the same currency. Keep silver-ticket and golden-ticket offers separate. At the guild merchant, contribute to bargaining first, then judge the final price. The reported 2,000-to-500-gem example was a 75% reduction; it does not promise that discount on every item.

## Protect free opportunities
Before saving tickets for an event, check whether the mode adds tickets every day or merely refills a low balance. Include ad attempts you may lose while stockpiling. A retained balance does not automatically mean extra free attempts.

## Basis of this plan
Shop and starter priorities reflect November 2026 guidance. Discount, fishing and refill examples are dated; check live listings and reset rules. No fixed daily gem income or guaranteed event return is established by these references.

articles.title: What to upgrade next: a progression roadmap
articles.summary: Follow reachable milestones for your main mode: starter gear, hero stars, etched slots, useful enchants and supporting collections. Reassess after each unlock.
articles.body:
## 1. Choose one main mode and a gear direction
Pick the activity you want to improve first. The November 2026 starting guidance favors Dragoon as an all-round direction and Oracle for PvE. Target that direction with Mythstone keys rather than changing plans after every drop. These are early recommendations, not permanent full-set requirements.

## 2. Work toward a reachable hero breakpoint
- Early PvP: Helix is the suggested rare option.
- PvE damage: Hou Yi is the suggested rare option.
- Movement: Nyanja is suggested when speed serves your goal.
Use the guild shop to work toward six stars on the chosen rare hero. Two six-star rares for different modes are a possible later plan; avoid judging an unfinished hero by bonuses it has not unlocked.

## 3. Build toward etched slots
Once the early hero milestone is addressed, compare blessing runes in the guild, Arena and GvG shops. Extra etched slots are the progression goal, not an arbitrary number of pulls. Count your existing runes and actual fusion progress.
After the third slot, pause automatic blessing-rune purchases. Compare epic hero shards, a second rare hero or Sacred Hall progression against your next need.

## 4. Buy damage your build can use
- Main-weapon single target: compare main-weapon crit enchants.
- Multiple targets: Sharp Arrow bounce serves a different job.
- Early PvE milestones: legendary Arrow of Echoes and rare Echo Scythe are separate targets.
- Support route: legendary Sprite's Awe with two right-side sprite runes is one option; it does not require every slot to be a sprite.
Choose one coherent package before spending on a new damage family. A high percentage on the wrong effect does not solve your bottleneck.

## 5. Compare supporting milestones
Artifacts: compare the next Heavenly Music set milestone, keeping Flute and Conch balanced, with survival your mode actually needs. October advice favors Demon King Eye over Blood for damage reduction; it does not establish a universal star target.
Mystlings: compare the next collection milestone and heart gain with another level on a single pet. Collection bonuses and active-skill effects can serve a different purpose from raw pet damage.

## 6. Rebuild only when the pieces are ready
List the exact items, rarities, enchants and support needed for the next set. Count what you own before committing keys or swapping orbs. Keep your working setup while preparing missing pieces; old 30–120-day transition schedules are examples, not deadlines.

## When to change priority
If you die before dealing damage, compare survivability before more theoretical damage. If you survive but miss the target, review the actual damage source and relevant enchants. If a milestone requires an unreachable skin or star level, choose a benefit you can unlock sooner. Revisit this sequence after meaningful unlocks; it is a conditional plan, not an instruction to buy every item at once.

articles.title: Build planner: bosses, waves and PvP
articles.summary: Choose a damage source, match enchants to the mode and save a complete preset. Includes a mixed-set route and checks before changing support.
articles.body:
## Start with the job, not the power score
Create separate saved presets for activities with different targets. A higher displayed power total can include effects that do nothing in the mode you are entering.
- Bosses: single-target damage plus enough survival to finish. Judge changes against the same boss over a comparable duration.
- Waves: coverage, multiple-target damage and crowd control. Bounce and elemental or circle effects serve a different purpose from boss-only damage.
- PvP/GvG: review enemy-player effects and survivability. Remove boss/minion-only enchants where they do not apply, even if power falls.

## Identify your main damage source
Use your results to decide whether damage mainly comes from the weapon, explosions, circles or another effect. Match enchants to that family. Sharp Arrow main-weapon crit does not automatically improve every damage component in a mixed Dragoon/Oracle build. Change one relevant enchant at a time when comparing.

## Gear direction and a mixed-set option
For an early account, November 2026 guidance suggests Dragoon as an all-round direction or Oracle for PvE. Work toward useful pieces rather than forcing a permanent full set.
An October mixed-set example uses Oracle chest, Griffin amulet and Dragoon in the other slots. Its purpose is combining explosion damage with sustain. Treat it as a candidate to test with your inventory, not a requirement to dismantle a stronger existing setup.

## Choose support you can actually assemble
- Sprite route: legendary Sprite's Awe with two right-side sprite runes supports another main damage source. You do not need to fill every slot with sprites.
- Plant route: verify rune rarity, enchants, etched support and any assumed Demeter setup before switching.
- Transition rule: retain working support until the replacement's required pieces are ready. Compare survival as well as damage.

## Plant enchant choices by role
September 2026 recommendations distinguish Vine Bind unique for PvE from plant damage for PvP. Rootguard unique is suggested for GvG, plant damage otherwise. Equinox Bloom and Plant Summon use unique enchants in the discussed setups, with damage alternatives in some hybrids. These are role-based choices; do not apply one enchant list to every mode.

## Save a complete preset
Record equipment, rune page, etched runes, enchants, hero, both resonances, Mystling and Close/Mid/Far behavior. Reopen the saved preset to verify it matches what you intended. A gear screenshot alone leaves important parts of the build unspecified.

## Keep or change?
Keep the new setup if it improves the goal you chose without unacceptable survival loss. If damage improves only in a shorter or easier fight, repeat under comparable conditions. Do not add several damage-taken reductions directly: the mixed-set discussion did not establish how those effects stack. The examples are recommendations from September–November 2026, not a complete tested preset for every rarity.

articles.title: Daily and weekly progression checklist
articles.summary: Protect free attempts, use energy for a purpose and keep guild participation organized. A repeatable routine without inventing fixed reward totals.
articles.body:
## Start each session: check what expires
1. Open the current tasks and active event screens. Note the actual reset or closing time.
2. Check ticket balances and refill rules before saving attempts. A mode may refill only when below its cap; carrying tickets can cost future free attempts.
3. Count available ad opportunities separately if you use them. Check privilege-card conditions instead of assuming every account has the same allowance.

## Spend energy according to today's goal
- Need runes and have time: compare your Hard Mode farming results.
- Need gear or gold and have time: compare a chapter you can clear reliably.
- Have little time: use Quick Hunt where available instead of planning manual runs you will not finish.
The October 2025 comparison favored Hard Mode 5 for runes, Chapter 47 for gear/gold and Quick Hunt for convenience. Use those as routes to compare, not guaranteed current drop rates. Its maxed drop talents and energy assumptions may differ from your account.

## Complete the guild actions that need coordination
Contribute to merchant bargaining before evaluating purchases. Check raid deadlines and use the participation attempt required by the current reward rules. Keep your expedition preset complete: gear, runes, hero, resonances, Mystling and distance behavior.
For raid leaders, announce the closing time and allow absent members to participate after an early boss clear where the current event permits it. Do not press a results button without checking whether it ends participation.

## Before ending the session
Check whether your next planned upgrade is now reachable. Claim the resources you earned, update the balance used by any event calculator and stop purchases once your target is secured. Save any changed preset; do not assume a test setup is your intended battle setup.

## Once a week: review the plan
1. Recount the exact pieces, hero shards and runes missing from your next milestone.
2. Review shop priorities: chosen rare hero, then etched-slot progression; reassess after the third slot.
3. Review comparable battle replays. Identify whether damage, positioning or early deaths are limiting progress.
4. Change one priority for the next week rather than spreading resources across every build idea.

## Before each event closes
Read retention or conversion text for each exact currency. Do not assume only dice can carry over, and do not assume every currency does. Spend or save according to the live rule, remaining stock and your target. This routine combines reviewed community advice; daily allowances, shops and event schedules still come from your current game screen.

articles.title: Event spending: choose a target and know when to stop
articles.summary: A decision guide for fishing, Treasure Island and event shops. Separate reward targets from gem costs, count free resources and avoid chasing sunk costs.
articles.body:
## Before the first purchase
Choose one exact reward from the current exchange. Note its currency, quantity, stock limit and closing time. Set a gem ceiling before random outcomes start influencing the decision. Count current resources and remaining free tasks; wait for relevant overlapping-event information when it could change the purchase.

## Match the route to the reward
- Fishing reward costs silver tickets: compare the silver-focused route, which aims to reach Polar with more lures for higher-value catches.
- Fishing reward costs golden tickets: compare the golden-focused route, which seeks additional legendaries in earlier lakes. It trades some silver-ticket progress for a lower historical gem budget; it is not a fixed-price guarantee.
- Treasure Island milestone: enter current tile, points, held dice and the in-game roll-task count into Dice Companion. Recalculate after meaningful changes instead of treating the initial estimate as a promise.

## Keep points and purchases separate
100,000 or 150,000 Treasure Island points are score targets, not gem budgets. The October 2026 comparison included extra shop-ticket purchases: eight earned tickets plus two purchases at 100,000 points, and a stated total of 20 at 150,000 when those purchases were included. Check the live track and prices before using those totals. An unlocked purchase is not a reward already owned.

## Use a buy-or-stop checkpoint
1. Read the next reward's actual requirement.
2. Subtract your current balance and free resources still realistically available.
3. Check the cost of the next small purchase against your remaining gem ceiling.
4. Buy only if the target is still worth that cost; update the calculation after the outcome.
5. Stop when the reward is secured, the ceiling is reached or the remaining target no longer justifies the cost.
Previous spending does not make the next purchase more valuable. Random catches and dice results can leave a target unfinished within your budget.

## Compare exchange offers fairly
For matching rewards paid in the same currency, divide price by bundle quantity and check stock. An archived fishing example lists five keys for 8,000 silver tickets, or 1,600 each; a separate premium listing uses four golden tickets for five keys. Do not compare those currency totals directly without a supported conversion model. Read today's listings.

## Closing-time decision
Check the retention or conversion rule for the exact currency, including future reruns. An Ancient Core carryover notice is a historical exception to an older dice-only claim; neither establishes every current currency's rule. Save only when the live text supports it. Otherwise assess useful remaining exchanges before the event closes.

## Use the detailed playbooks
The fishing playbook explains pools, line breaks and both routes. The Treasure Island playbook explains departure tiles, multiplier caps and calculator inputs. Their models guide decisions; they do not replace current event rules or guarantee a target.

articles.title: Jungle upgrades: check stage skips before raising rating
articles.summary: Inspect blessing strength, reward blocks and automatic clears before making a large rune-rating upgrade.
articles.body:
## Before upgrading
1. Check the current Jungle Blessing description and next rating threshold.
2. Compare manual-stage rewards with automatic-clear rewards.
3. Make an incremental upgrade if a large jump would skip rewards you still need.

## Historical optimization
July 2025 notes describe orange blessing at 200% ATK/HP versus purple at 20%, Enchantium rewards in ten-stage blocks and a target stage ending in 1. The goal was retaining the stronger blessing while preserving manually earned tickets.

## Recheck first
These values are historical. A linked calculator, edited February 3, 2026, was labeled work in progress with uncertain higher-tier values. Its cells and the blessing image were not checked. Current thresholds and skipped-stage rewards require an in-game check.

articles.title: Jungle circles: choose enchants around Sawblade rarity
articles.summary: Use separate enchant plans before and after mythic Sawblade; prioritize circle control before secondary damage.
articles.body:
## Starting framework
The June 2026 recipe without twin runes names both circle runes, Frostshock Seal and Root Guard on the left, with Pulsing, Orbital and Awe as etched choices. The right-side page is image-dependent and is not fully reconstructed here.

## Choose the appropriate branch
- Before mythic Sawblade: one mythic circle crit-rate enchant, Flamenox unique, then boss damage; Frostshock unique is another option.
- With mythic Sawblade: Sawblade unique plus circle spin speed and damage.
- Skills: circle effects, especially freeze, then fire/poison; sprites and attack boosts follow.

## Check the correction
A July 1 edit says Sawblade uses global crit stats rather than main-weapon crit, replacing Sharp Arrow with boss damage. This remains unverified. October twin-rune comments do not establish a complete updated preset; recheck before investing.

articles.title: Elemental Jungle: check the enchant prerequisites
articles.summary: Match the recipe's Domain, elemental crit and enchant requirements before committing to an elemental build.
articles.body:
## Recipe requirements
The June 6, 2026 setup specifies:
- Domain L1 and elemental crit L1, preferably L2 for both.
- Two 30% elemental crit-rate enchants.
- Two 30% elemental-damage enchants.
- Ring of Agony unique enchant.

These are requirements for this recipe, not universal minimums.

## Skill priorities
Prioritize elemental effects, especially rings, tracking, Split Shot and Pierce. Additional arrow skills and Short Range are suggested; Swift Arrow supports elemental procs. Bounce helps crowded waves, while boss damage serves a different target.

## Lower-investment starting route
A separate starter recipe uses charged rings, piercing, Lightwing and arrow upgrades, with freeze/lightning for control. It is not proven equivalent. Complete screenshots and current patch behavior were not checked.

articles.body:

1. Identify whether damage comes mainly from the weapon, explosions, circles or another effect.
2. Check which damage family each enchant names.
3. Compare equal-duration runs against the same target with only the enchant changed.

## October 2026 guidance
A discussion comparing 30% Sharp Arrow crit rate with 15% boss damage explicitly limits the crit enchant to main-weapon damage. Its favorable boss recommendation concerned a main-weapon setup, not every mixed Dragoon/Oracle build.

## Arena caveat
Later comments qualify its value in advanced Arena setups while allowing uses for main-weapon crit. No controlled results establish a universal winner. A larger displayed percentage is not automatically a better upgrade.

articles.title: Farming choices: Quick Hunt, Hard Mode 5 or Chapter 47
articles.summary: Compare loot goals against time available. Historical tables favor different routes for runes, gear and convenience.
articles.body:
## Choose your goal
- Runes per run: the October 2025 comparison favored Hard Mode 5.
- Gear and gold: Chapter 47 was favored in the written results.
- Limited time: Quick Hunt offered the most convenient route.

## What the old table models
With maxed gear/rune-drop talents and 145 energy daily for 30 days, Chapter 47 projects 1,740 gear pieces versus 1,066 from Quick Hunt. Rune totals are 1,679 versus 1,066. The printed rune difference is 612, although those totals subtract to 613.

## Keep assumptions separate
The 51 hours versus 15 minutes compares modeled completion/action time; Quick Hunt assumes one second per action, not total monthly playtime. Adjacent 165-energy columns are a different scenario. Both tables were visually reviewed, but their projections are not current drop guarantees.

articles.title: Guild Merchant: bargain together before buying
articles.summary: Help reduce the displayed price, then judge the final purchase against your current progression goal.
articles.body:
## Buying checklist
1. Check the current bargain state.
2. Complete your available bargaining contribution before purchases.
3. Recheck the final item, currency and price.
4. Buy only if the reward supports your current goal.

## Discount example
March 2026 guidance reports collective participation reducing a 2,000-gem item to 500 gems: a 75% reduction.

## Keep the limit clear
That example does not prove every item always receives a 75% discount. Item screenshots and the current cap were not independently checked. A discount alone does not make a purchase the best use of gems.

articles.title: Rumble milestones: spread trophies across heroes
articles.summary: An April 2026 route targets 450 trophies through three heroes near 150 each. Check separate tracks and daily tasks.
articles.body:
## Historical milestone route
The April 2026 plan targets 450 total trophies by bringing three heroes to roughly 150 each. It favors lower trophy ranges because they were described as easier and without loss penalties in that range.

## Keep progression tracks separate
Geared and ungeared modes were described as having separate milestone rewards. The guide also recommended three daily runs for then-current tasks, even after finishing milestones.

## Before committing time
Check today's milestone screen, loss rules and daily tasks. Carryover into later events was claimed, but is not confirmed for current rules. Supporting videos and reward images were not checked; the route is a dated planning option.

articles.title: Plant Defense: level up before rushing progress orbs
articles.summary: Prioritize archers and balance faster completion against time needed to gain levels.
articles.body:
## Control the main threat
The May 2026 approach circles the plant, watches recurring archer spawn positions and uses ice control. Rolla resonance is one suggested option, not a universal requirement.

## Decide when to collect white orbs
White orbs were reported to advance the progress bar and shorten the run. If survival is uncertain, delaying collection can preserve time to gain levels. Once your setup is strong enough, faster progress may help.

## Recheck the tradeoff
A six-minute to four-minute improvement was an individual observation, not a timing guarantee. Videos were not reviewed, so exact positioning and a full preset are not reconstructed. Adapt orb timing to the current mode and your survival margin.

articles.title: Mystlings: compare collection milestones with single-pet levels
articles.summary: Evaluate collection gains and active-skill effects before concentrating every resource into one Mystling.
articles.body:
## Before upgrading
Compare the next collection milestone, heart gain and active-skill description with the benefit of another level on one pet.

## Collection versus concentration
May 2026 guidance describes collection leveling as providing hearts and account-wide bonuses, including active-skill cooldown improvements. Heavy investment in one pet was described as mainly increasing its skill damage. No complete scaling table is available here.

## Use relevant active skills
Some setups gain offensive or defensive stacking buffs through activations. Activate those skills promptly when their current description supports it; do not transfer one setup's percentages to every Mystling.

The illustrated skills and linked progression workbook were not independently checked. Use actual in-game milestones rather than assuming every upgrade has equal value.

articles.title: Jungle sprites: main damage or support?
articles.summary: Choose whether sprites are your damage engine or support through Sprite's Awe; each plan needs different skill priorities.
articles.body:
## Choose one primary plan
- Sprite-focused: invest in sprite damage, then address crowded waves with a secondary circle or elemental-domain component.
- Support-focused: use Sprite's Awe to support another main damage source without filling every slot with sprites.

## Crowded-stage tradeoff
The June 2026 domain variation was described as safer against bosses than dense waves. It needed enough elemental damage to trigger clearing reliably, with a warning against going beyond green difficulty without the discussed L+2 Domain investment.

## Update before copying
October discussion still referenced sprite frameworks, while a later warning said Twinborn runes changed builds. Exact slots were partly image-dependent and no patch version is stated. Treat this as a planning distinction, not a complete current preset.

articles.title: Build separate presets for bosses, waves and PvP
articles.summary: Match enchants, survival and behavior to the actual mode instead of chasing one maximum power score.
articles.body:
## Preset checklist
- Bosses: prioritize relevant single-target damage and enough survival to finish.
- Waves: account for multiple targets, coverage and control.
- PvP/GvG: review effects that only apply to bosses or minions before entering.

## Test in the intended mode
August 2026 discussion gives an example boss preset without bounce, shield or dodge choices. That is specialization, not proof those effects are always useless.

Repeated GvG guidance warns that boss/minion enchants do not help those fights, even when removing them lowers displayed power.

## Final check
Save each preset, verify its active hero and enchants, then compare actual results. Best choices depend on available upgrades and current mechanics.

articles.title: Twinborn crafting: check category, tier and both currencies
articles.summary: Ability and enhancement examples cannot be applied automatically to blessing or etched runes.
articles.body:
## Before crafting
1. Select the exact rune category and tier in the current crafting screen.
2. Check both core and remnant requirements.
3. Count resources for the complete planned upgrade, not only the first craft.

## September 2026 examples
Reported ability/enhancement examples use Legendary +2 at 5,000 remnants and mythic at 40 cores plus 20,000 remnants. Blessing and etched runes were explicitly described as needing more cores.

## Important limits
Legendary +1 eligibility was speculation. These examples are not a complete cost table. Remnants may become the bottleneck even when cores are available, depending on inventory. The crafting image was not reviewed; verify the recipe before spending.

articles.title: Expedition lanes: plan matchups, then review replays
articles.summary: Choose lane concentration from the opposing roster and use replays to evaluate behavior, survival and damage.
articles.body:
## Plan the formation
1. Compare the opposing lanes and available roster.
2. Decide whether spreading strength across three lanes or concentrating on fewer offers better matchups.
3. Record behavior presets and the formation used.

## Review the result
Watch replays from comparable battles. Check whether positioning, control or early deaths explain the outcome before judging only by total damage.

## Unresolved mechanic
March 2026 discussion suggests lane members benefit from the strongest gear/artifacts in their team, motivating distribution of well-equipped players. No formula is provided, so do not calculate a shared-stat bonus from this claim.

Roster images were not analyzed. These are planning practices, not one optimal formation.

articles.title: Meteor builds: complete the survival engine before switching
articles.summary: Check potion generation, shielding and hero support before judging a crossbow or Dragoon conversion.
articles.body:
## Conversion checklist
- Confirm the potion effects and cooldown enchants the plan relies on.
- Check whether Potion Spring and potion shielding are sufficiently upgraded.
- Compare the relevant hero and skin support.
- Test survival as well as damage against similar opponents.

## Why support matters
November 2026 discussion links weaker survival after a proposed switch to missing Otta, Potion Spring and potion-shield support. The explanation was explicitly theoretical. Earlier advice favored an Otta skin for a potion-dependent setup, not as a universal first purchase.

## Evidence limit
No controlled win-rate comparison establishes the best hero, weapon or skin. The pictured loadout was not reviewed. Copying one item without its supporting effects may produce different results.

articles.title: Mixed Dragoon: preserve sustain while changing sets
articles.summary: An October 2026 recipe keeps Oracle chest and Griffin amulet, then chooses plant or sprite support around available upgrades.
articles.body:
## Example mixed set
The October 24 recipe uses Oracle chest, Griffin amulet and Dragoon in the other slots. Its aim is balancing explosion damage with sustain, rather than maximizing one set bonus at any cost.

## Match rune support to resources
- Consider plants where the required rarities and enchants are available.
- Otherwise, right-side sprites with Sprite's Awe form another support package.
- Compare shielding and survival before replacing an established circle setup.

## Test the whole change
A proposed 80% total from several damage-taken effects was explicitly uncertain about diminishing returns. Do not assume those effects add directly. articles.title: Event currencies: check carryover item by item
articles.summary: The old dice-only carryover rule has exceptions. Read each currency's current conversion or retention text.
articles.body:
## Before an event ends
1. Identify the exact currency name.
2. Read its current carryover or conversion rule.
3. Check whether that rule applies to future reruns of the same event.
4. Save or spend according to that currency's rule, not a blanket event rule.

## Known historical exception
An old guide says only Treasure Hunt dice and Treasure Coins carry over. An August 26, 2025 hotfix notice says Ancient Cores can carry into later summoning events, starting with the August 30-September 5 event.

## What this establishes
The dice-only statement is too broad, even though the guide was edited later. This exception does not establish current retention rules for every currency or future event.

articles.title: Archived boss build: Tracking Eye, rings and crit triggers
articles.summary: A March 2026 Monster Invasion/Seal recipe requires Thor 5 stars and an Oracle-heavy mixed set.
articles.body:
## Required setup
The March 4, 2026 recipe uses Tracking Eye, energy rings and Lightwing, with at least Thor 5 stars for its lightning-critical interaction.

## Equipment and rune priorities
- Dragoon weapon, Oracle amulet and Griffin ring.
- Oracle helmet, chest and boots.

articles.title: Treasure Island: when to roll ×1 or ×10
articles.summary: Use the numbered departure map, check your held dice and estimate your target with Dice Companion. A practical walkthrough of the September 2025 model, with its limits clearly marked.
articles.body:
## The quick rule
In the linked Dice Companion model, use the high multiplier when you are standing on tile 8, 9, 20, 21 or 22. Use ×1 from all other tiles. Numbers run from 0 to 23; tile 0 is Start.

Choose the multiplier BEFORE rolling, using your current departure tile. These are not instructions to land on those tiles using ×10. Check your new position after every roll. Compare the diagram with the live board first: this is a September 2025 model, not a verified rule for every event rotation.

## Play one move at a time
1. Choose the reward milestone you actually want and set a spending limit.
2. Collect dice already earned from tasks and rewards.
3. Locate your current tile on the numbered map.
4. On a highlighted departure tile, use the model's high multiplier only if your held dice and the live toggle allow it. Otherwise use ×1.
5. Roll once, collect the result, then locate the new tile before choosing again.
6. Recheck your actual score, next reward and remaining dice before extending your target.

## Dice limits in this model
- 0 dice: collect more before rolling.
- 1–19 dice: maximum ×1.
- 20–29 dice: maximum ×2.
- 30–49 dice: maximum ×3.
- 50–99 dice: maximum ×5.
- 100 or more dice: maximum ×10.
These caps only raise the recommendation on highlighted tiles. Other tiles stay at ×1. The older discussion used different thresholds and fewer highlighted tiles; do not combine maps. Check your actual in-game controls.

## What ×10 does
The model spends ten dice on one movement outcome and scales that landing reward. It is not ten independent trips around the board. A poor landing uses more of your saved dice at once, so reaching a target is never guaranteed.

## Use Dice Companion
Open Dice Companion from Links & references. For a run already underway, use Success Rate Calculator: enter Goal Points, dice currently held, Current Tile, Current Points and Rolls Done. Claim earned dice first so your inputs match the screen.

Use the in-game task counter for Rolls Done, not the number of times you pressed the roll button. In the model, a ×10 roll advances that counter by ten. Recalculate after meaningful changes to your score or available dice.

Should I Roll? estimates a starting budget from a target score and desired success chance. It uses a different simulation setup that does not enforce low-dice multiplier caps during each simulated run. Treat its result as an estimate; use the actual-state calculator to assess dice you really hold.

## Score is not gem cost
100k and 150k mean event points. Shop tickets unlocked by those scores can still require a separate gem purchase. Read the current reward track and shop before comparing value per ticket. A score milestone does not establish a fixed dice or gem budget.

## Model limits
The tool runs random simulations with a fixed board and reward assumptions. Results can vary between calculations; they are not official drop probabilities. Its source was last updated in September 2025 when checked on November 3, 2026. Current game behavior has not been tested here. The older Treasure Hunt page is explicitly unmaintained and directs readers to Dice Companion.

articles.title: Fishing: pools, line breaks and ticket routes
articles.summary: Track what remains in each lake, choose a silver- or golden-ticket route, and save selective line breaks for the catches that matter.
articles.body:
## Start with your reward
Choose the item you want from the exchange, note whether it costs silver or golden tickets, and set a gem ceiling. Count free lures still available from current tasks before buying more. Purchase extra lures in small batches and stop when your actual ticket balance reaches the target.

## Understand the pool
Normal Lakehouse, Sunset Coast and Oceanic Abyss pools contain 40 fish: 30 rare, 9 epic and 1 legendary. Polar Glacier doubles that to 80: 60 rare, 18 epic and 2 legendary. Each lake keeps its own remaining fish. The pool refills after all fish in that pool have been caught.
- Catching removes a fish from its pool.
- Breaking a line returns that fish to the pool. It does not create another legendary or advance the refill.
- A new lake has its own pool; revisiting an earlier lake resumes its remaining fish.
- Count fish landed, not button presses. Four complete x10 catches account for 40 fish. Catch order is still random.

## When to use x10 or break a line
Use x10 when you intend to finish a complete pool. Switch to smaller casts when approaching a lake transition or your final partial pool. Track whether a legendary or useful epic still remains before spending breaks.
If you will catch the whole pool anyway, a break only postpones catching that fish. Selective breaks help when you intend to leave some fish behind. Once your target legendary is caught, catch the fish needed to progress instead of repeatedly rejecting the same depleted pool.
The simpler selective method uses x1. A March 2026 route uses x2 and rejects rare-only batches while keeping epics and legendaries; this requires reading the whole batch correctly. Check your remaining exchange allowance before every selective session: the collected guides describe 120 refundable broken lines, not unlimited free retries.

## Route A: prioritize silver tickets
This route tries to reach Polar with more lures available for its higher-value catches.
1. Lakehouse: clear one full pool. Target the second legendary and epics in the next pool, then catch what is needed to unlock Sunset.
2. Sunset: clear two full pools. Target the third legendary and epics, then progress to Oceanic.
3. Oceanic: clear two full pools. Target the third legendary and epics, then progress to Polar.
4. Polar: clear complete 80-fish pools while pursuing your chosen ticket goal. Reserve remaining breaks for valuable fish in your final partial pool.

## Route B: prioritize golden tickets
This route seeks additional legendaries in earlier lakes, accepting fewer silver tickets in exchange for a lower historical gem budget.
1. Lakehouse: clear two full pools. Revisit after unlocking Sunset if needed, then use x1 selective catches to seek a third legendary.
2. Sunset: clear two full pools, seek the third legendary, then progress.
3. Oceanic: clear three full pools. Revisit after unlocking Polar if needed and use x1 to seek a fourth legendary.
4. Polar: clear two full pools, then use your remaining breaks to seek the two legendaries in the next pool.
The normal-lake target is 3 + 3 + 4 + 6 legendary catches. Lures or refundable breaks can run out before you finish; this is a route, not a guaranteed 16-legendary run.

## Read tension with the correct rod
Look at initial tension when the fish bites. Compare it only with examples for the same rod and lake: stronger rods lower tension and later lakes increase it. Resistance colors describe behavior and should not be used alone as a universal rarity code. Practice with x1 before rejecting a batch.
The linked early-lake comparison uses the final rod in lakes 1-3. The separate Polar comparison uses an epic rod. Those screenshots are different references, not interchangeable thresholds.

## Use the Fishing Companion
1. Open Fishing Companion from References and select your current lake and matching fish artwork.
2. Set the actual cast multiplier before logging. Tap each fish landed; the app groups the results into that cast.
3. Use Undo for mistakes. Track broken lines separately instead of removing released fish from the pool.
4. Choose the gold- or silver-focused plan by its description. Option numbers differ between older guides and tools.
5. Check actual in-game weight and ticket balance before changing lakes or spending. The tool estimates weight; its break advice is a model, not proof of an optimal cast. Progress saves in that browser only.

## Dragon Gate and Fullmoon
These are special event pools, separate from the normal lake. Select the correct special pool in the tracker and keep its counts separate. Check the event's own visit limit and shard rewards. Reports disagree about selectively breaking rare fish there; catching its fish is the conservative approach until your rotation's rules are clear. Do not apply normal 40/80-fish refill logic automatically to a limited special-pool visit.

## Version notes
The routes come from a March 2026 guide; October 2026 replies reaffirm the normal pool sizes and early-lake filtering approach. The linked tracker was updated in October 2026. No current game build was tested here. Check live task requirements, rod behavior, exchange limits and special-pool rules before committing resources. Archived gem estimates are intentionally omitted because costs depend on actual catches and event changes.

articles.title: Croc boss: control the summons and keep damage flowing
articles.summary: A practical control package for Croc: ice, paralysis or Thor, bounce for summoned enemies and vines. Choose each part for its job.
articles.body:
## What this setup is trying to solve
Croc adds a second job to the fight: deal with summoned enemies while continuing to damage the boss. An October 2026 recommendation combines crowd control with multi-target coverage. Use that package as a starting preset when the adds are the reason your run fails.

## The four components
- Ice / Super Ice: the suggested freeze options.
- Paralysis rune or Thor at five stars: the proposed control option. The five-star requirement belongs to the Thor option; do not assume an unfinished Thor supplies the same effect.
- Bounce support, described as "4 bounce": included specifically to finish the minions. This describes the bounce effect, not a requirement to equip four bounce runes. This is why a Croc preset can justify bounce even when your usual single-boss preset drops it.
- Vines: another suggested control component. The unique enchant was also recommended, without a complete enchant-rarity table.

## Assemble the preset before the attempt
1. Start from the damage setup you can already sustain against this boss.
2. Add the ice package and choose the paralysis or five-star Thor route you actually own.
3. Keep the bounce component if summoned enemies remain the bottleneck.
4. Add vines when available, then check whether the required effects survived saving the preset.
5. Review the next attempt for two separate outcomes: how quickly adds disappear and how much damage reaches Croc.

## Adjust the part that is failing
If adds remain alive, compare the multi-target and control package before adding more boss-only damage. If adds die comfortably but Croc remains healthy, compare your main damage source without removing every control tool at once. This adjustment sequence is a way to use the listed package, not a recorded fixed rotation.

## Scope
The source identifies useful skills for this matchup; it does not provide a complete gear rarity, damage requirement or dodge-timing guide. Treat the October 2026 package as conditional advice for your inventory.

This is a close-range route for the Flame Demon guild boss. The April 2025 report describes moving around the boss and collecting experience as it moves. Its damage package is designed around staying near the target, not treating every ranged skill as interchangeable.

## Supporting runes
The same report used double-experience and revive runes. Experience support is meant to reach the skill package sooner; revive provides another opportunity to continue if the attempt fails. Neither removes the need to survive the boss's attacks.

## Run the route
1. Prepare the experience and revive support available to your account.
2. Build toward the circle-and-flame package during skill selection.
3. Move around the boss while gathering dropped experience as the boss changes position.
4. Judge the melee sprite in that close-range route. A run spent far from the target is testing a different plan.
5. Afterward, separate a missing-skill problem from a survival problem before changing the whole preset.

## When to use another plan
If approaching the boss causes repeated early deaths, this recipe is a poor match for that attempt. Preserve a setup you can survive with while comparing the close-range option. The source does not establish a minimum health, exact damage reduction or mandatory hero.

## Date and limits
This is the corrected April 2025 recipe, retained as a concrete matchup option. No later controlled comparison in the reviewed evidence establishes it as the current best Flame Demon build. Check the live boss and your available skill effects before investing resources solely for it.

articles.summary: A concrete eight-rune framework, its circle alternatives, and the Cleo/Otta enchant recommendations behind a Dragoon potion setup.
articles.body:
## Pick one eight-rune framework
An April 2026 discussion gives three specific starting layouts for 1v1:
- Four meteor runes plus four elemental runes.
- Four circle runes plus four elemental runes.
- Four circle runes plus two weapon runes and the left-side lightning/ice pair.
These are alternative layouts. Do not add all three together or copy the rune count without checking the associated gear and etched support. The discussion favors the meteor/elemental direction for its Dragoon PvP example; the circle alternatives belong to a different damage plan.

## Match the package to the target
Four-bounce weapon support was suggested for 3v3 coverage, with an immediate qualification: it loses value when the opponent's lineup revolves around one strong hero and two supporting heroes. For a single boss, a later message drops bounce. Choose coverage for targets that actually exist in the fight.

## The Phynx, Otta and Cleo example
September advice describes Phynx with Otta and Cleo resonances, using elemental and meteor runes instead of the main-weapon package. The follow-up explicitly asks about resonances before choosing enchants. Treat the hero package as part of the recipe; an account without the potion support is not assembling the same build.

## Enchant priorities from that example
1. With Cleo/Otta, compare the unique enchants on both left-side elemental runes.
2. The right-side fire rune also receives a unique-enchant recommendation.
3. The response names 25% cooldown and 30% additional meteor damage as alternatives. It does not identify the precise cooldown tooltip in text; check the linked preset and your rune before spending enchant resources.
4. Work toward the unique strike-potion enchant. The advice also proposes changing right-side weapon runes and Potion Spring, but the exact replacement slots depend on the linked preset images. Verify those slots before removing a working support effect.
An earlier discussion separately emphasizes the right-side unique meteor enchant that triggers giant meteors when taking damage. It is a different effect from simply choosing more elemental damage.

## Upgrade in stages
Save your working preset first. Add the functional support you own, then compare one enchant change at a time against similar opponents. If the potion package is incomplete, finish or retain a coherent alternative before swapping the weapon and expecting the same survival. Keep etched circle investment available for a circle/boss preset rather than treating a PvP change as a reason to discard it.

## What this ranks
This guide prioritizes components within specific 1v1 and potion-oriented setups. It does not establish a universal weapon tier list, an exact win-rate gain or a complete best-in-slot answer for every rarity. The layouts come from April 2026; the detailed resonance/enchant discussion is from September 2026.

articles.summary: The specific sprite-focused route: etched prerequisites, mandatory support, skill selection order and the crowded-wave tradeoff.
articles.body:
## Decide whether sprites lead or support
The June 2026 guide distinguishes two jobs. With two sprite etched runes, sprites are the main damage plan and sprite upgrades are priorities. With only Sprite's Awe supporting circles or elements, choose the primary damage package first; do not spend every selection on sprite buffs merely because Awe is equipped.

## Sprite + Domain recipe
The stated example recommends Cleo and lists:
- Two sprite etched runes plus one elemental etched rune.
- The rune abbreviated RoA in the source preset; confirm its identity in the linked loadout.
- Four sprites.
- Plant shielding after green difficulty, described as required for this route.
- An additional elemental choice when it helps secure the kill needed to activate Domain pools.
The text does not identify every image-dependent rune slot. Check the linked preset and your inventory before treating this as a complete eight-slot screenshot replacement.

## Skill pick order for the sprite-led version
1. Sprites.
2. Sprite-enhancing skills.
3. Super Freeze.
4. Elemental skills.
5. Attack Speed.
6. Attack Power.
This is the order proposed for this specific route. It is not a general ranking for a circle-led, weapon-led or PvP build. If Awe is only support, return to your main damage priorities instead.

## Blessing and survival support
Experience support is marked as essential in the recipe. Revive is included, with luck or dodge as optional choices in the discussion. A Rabbit Foot slot was explained as an enchant choice; do not assume the rune's normal effect is required for Jungle or rely on a universal luck-to-proc formula.

## Check the Domain breakpoint before spending
The guide warns against taking the Domain version beyond green without the investment it calls Domain L2. Its problem is crowded waves: insufficient elemental damage can fail to secure the kill that starts the clearing effect. The same account described the route as safer against bosses and circles as easier when that Domain investment was missing.

## Choose the route that fits your account
Use the sprite/Domain plan when its etched and elemental requirements are ready. If dense waves remain the failure point, compare a circle-supported sprite route rather than buying random upgrades from several families. Keep the test conditions comparable and check survival before interpreting a higher damage number as progress.

## Current-use limit
The detailed recipe dates to June 2026. October discussion still referenced sprite frameworks, but an October 30 warning says Twinborn runes changed Jungle builds. Retain the skill-selection logic as a reference; verify current rune interactions and rarity requirements before a major conversion.
